arguments.literal: A bounded context exists only when an owning authority declares its stable identity, owner, selected basis and governed semantic scope. A consuming member may define a concept inside that context only through an explicit owner relation. A filename, heading, index row, glossary section, schema value or bare URI cannot constitute the context. A document, section, schema field, operation or other owning surface may declare a context for all its subordinate occurrences, so uniquely resolved prose need not repeat a qualifier on every term; a repository, directory, filename, heading, glossary match, prompt, actor or nearby definition does not declare a bounded context by accident.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P6

A cross-context relation is explicit and owner-authorised. Its carrier states: the exact source and target concept references and bounded-context identities; whether it imports unchanged meaning, disambiguates a use, translates directionally (a specialisation included) or establishes the stronger equivalence claim; its direction and any lawful inverse where material; the preserved meaning, changed meaning, loss and refusal conditions; the source and target semantic owners, without transferring either authority; the selected source and target bases, the governed scope and provenance; and its lifecycle and invalidation conditions.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P4b, P6

A Semantic Import adopts the cited meaning unchanged for its declared target scope. A Semantic Translation declares how meaning changes in one direction. Semantic Equivalence requires the governing authorities to establish the claimed equality; neither identical spelling nor two opposing translations proves it automatically. A Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. No relation widens its source or target authority. A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding target-context constraints. It identifies the exact target concept, the preserved and narrowed meaning, the excluded source instances, and the absence or law of any inverse. Calling a term a specialisation without those coordinates establishes nothing. Each local_constitution.disambiguations binding additionally names: term: the exact lexical label being resolved; context: the bounded-context identity in which the resolution applies; disambiguates: the complete material candidate concept or clause references; resolves_to: the exact selected concept reference, which is one member of disambiguates; basis: every selected semantic basis needed to interpret the candidates and the resolution; and uri, authority and applies_to: the owning resolution carrier, the lawful authority and the exact governed scope. The referenced uri owns the resolution. When the candidates cross bounded contexts, that carrier also declares the complete import, translation or equivalence relation §5 requires. The overlay metadata makes the relation discoverable and checkable; it neither restates the source-owned meanings nor mints the decision.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution, §6 Local constitutional binding; P1, P3, P6

The glossary (the GLOSSARY member) is a non-deciding locator index. It contains no semantic definition and declares no bounded context, concept, import, translation, equivalence, disambiguation or authority. Each row records an indexed spelling, the bounded-context identity declared by the cited owning clause, and the exact owning concept clause; the owning clause with the selected basis identifies the candidate meaning, and the occurrence being resolved still supplies its own governed scope. An indexed concept applies only when the semantic address selects its owning clause or the target context explicitly imports it; appearance in the glossary creates no shared default. Repeated spellings in different rows are intentional; equal spelling, nearness in the index, a heading or inclusion creates no identity, inheritance, import, equivalence or authority. A row whose context or owning clause does not resolve is invalid and the index cannot repair it or a missing declaration; every locus is a clause of the current corpus, never of the predecessor cut; a term without an owning clause is not a valid row. Resolution follows PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5; the index supplies no fallback decision.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5; GLOSSARY §1 Index contract, §2 Locator law; P1, P3, P5, P6

product.bounded_context identifies the enclosing bounded context of the definition's own product WHAT, or is null when no separate enclosing context is claimed. It is not an exhaustive registry and does not flatten subordinate, peer, composed, tenant, user or runtime contexts into one namespace. Those contexts stay defined by their owning authorities, and every local disambiguation names the exact context in which its resolution applies.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations; P1, P3

Each definition contains: product: the stable product-definition identity, display name, source-project locator and an explicit bounded-context declaration or null; constitution.stdo: the STDO source repository, the mutable version-line discovery selector, and the exact installed release basis with its deterministic manifest digest; constitution.additional_authorities: every non-STDO constitutional set; constitution.entrypoints: basis-qualified useful reading routes; constitution.agent_bootstrap: the constitutional entrypoint and the marker-managed agent-instruction targets; local_constitution: local axioms, overrides and disambiguations with their owning authority, target, basis and scope, including context-qualified term resolution where applicable; reference_frame_bases: one or more accepted collective reference-frame basis declarations with their admitting authorities and governed scopes; what: the current Intent, Product and specification bindings; how: any shared realisation surfaces and one or more independent build tenants; ticketing: the Goals, ticket, comment and optional sprint carrier bindings; composition: explicit relations to other product definitions; and $schema and kind: the schema locator and the stdo.product-definition discriminator.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations; P3, P6

The overlay owns its locator and relation map; the referenced documents own their content. Repeating source truth inside the JSON creates a rival authority and is non-conformant. A local axiom, override or disambiguation gains no authority from its file category or from being listed in the overlay; every local entry names the URI carrying the local decision, the lawful authority that owns it (Product, requirement, accepted design or other), the clause or ambiguity it overrides or resolves where applicable, and its exact scope. An empty local array explicitly declares that no local entry of that kind is bound; omission is not an equivalent declaration.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §2 Required definition relations, §6 Local constitutional binding; P4b, P6

Without an explicit cross-context relation: Frame (reference-frame evaluation context vs a consumer-owned runtime carrier) remains distinct, nominal match cannot enrol the runtime carrier as an evaluation frame; Owner (generic specialist evaluation family vs a semantic or decision authority owner) remains distinct, the family acquires no owner authority; Product (immutable released Product vs mutable Product Definition) remains distinct and selects only through the occurrence's declared context; Tenant (STDO build realisation vs hosted, customer, account, runtime or data tenancy) remains distinct, build tenancy supplies no default; User (Product role, human person, identity principal, account, actor, operator or data subject) is unresolved until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates the meanings. A positive local case declares one context and resolves exactly one concept; a positive cross-context case supplies the complete authorised relation. Negative cases: zero candidates, multiple candidates after disambiguation, a selected concept outside the candidate set, a context-free glossary fallback, incomplete relation coordinates, authority or basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidated relations. Correct downstream behaviour produced through a guessed meaning does not pass semantic conformance.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §10 Semantic-resolution conformance cases; P1, P6

This member owns this law in the bounded context urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution under the selected complete STDO basis; a glossary may index that identity and does not participate in its declaration. A term is a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept identity. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope in which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly interpretable under named authority. A concept reference is an exact, resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected basis; it locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor its authority.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P3, P6

Every material term occurrence resolves under the semantic address (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope). Equal spelling, capitalisation, shape, file location, directory nesting, actor or implementation does not establish equal meaning, concept identity, equivalence, inheritance or authority; different spelling does not prove different meaning. Those relations follow only from the applicable semantic address or from an explicit authorised relation. Resolution proceeds in order: (1) identify the occurrence's governed scope and nearest explicit bounded-context declaration; (2) identify the exact selected basis and the authorities applicable to that context and scope; (3) collect the context-local definitions and the explicitly imported concept references admitted by those authorities and that basis; (4) apply every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; (5) admit the occurrence only when exactly one concept remains.
PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 Bounded-context semantic resolution; P1, P3, P5

Zero applicable concepts is unresolved meaning; more than one is ambiguous meaning. Both fail closed at a material boundary: an agent, design, schema, implementation, test, translation or reviewer must not select one by familiarity, frequency, recency, nominal match or a context-free glossary fallback.

symbols.label: Glossary: a non-deciding locator index from indexed spellings to the owning clauses that declare their bounded contexts and own their concepts
product.bounded_context: the enclosing bounded context of the definition's own product WHAT, or null
Local disambiguation: a local_constitution.disambiguations binding that selects one concept for one term in one bounded context and scope
Product definition: the stdo.product-definition overlay, the locator and relation map of one product whose referenced documents own their content
Semantic address: (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope)
Semantic authority: the owner of meaning for a material relation
Bounded context: an explicitly identified semantic scope in which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly interpretable under named authority
Concept reference: an exact, resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected basis
Cross-context relation: an explicit owner-authorised Semantic Import, Translation (specialisation included), Equivalence or Disambiguation between concepts of two bounded contexts
Term: a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept identity
